clue.text: Conceal second parent

parts.note: a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: Someone hides the fact that a second parent exists.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to stifle or suppress it, keeping it hidden from view.

clue.text: Boy to race around with motorcycle attachment

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of race are turned about

explanation.surface: A lad goes racing about on a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a one-wheeled passenger car fixed to the side of a motorbike.

clue.text: Gold tends to appear in French city

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
to lean towards is to tend to

explanation.surface: Gold is often found in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a city on the Loire.

clue.text: The osprey flies — look at that!

indicators.note: flies suggests the letters of the phrase take wing and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as an osprey takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's exclamation announcing a trick's surprising result.

clue.text: Soldiers' uniform is correct

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
dress means uniform, as in full dress

explanation.surface: The troops' kit is pronounced correct.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to put it right.

clue.text: Poor manners of naughty class

parts.note: a naughty child is bad
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A badly behaved school class shows a lack of manners.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM is the British word for a school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad form is an idiom for socially unacceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Fishmonger's offering to take money in his straw hat

indicators.note: in tells us the money letter goes inside the hat

parts.note: a boater is a flat straw hat
L stands for pound, money in Britain

explanation.surface: A fishmonger pockets cash in the straw hat he wears.
explanation.walkthrough: Traditional British fishmongers wore straw boaters; L (from Latin libra) is the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a whole smoked herring sold by fishmongers.

clue.text: Spot the king's lover

parts.note: a dot is a spot
ER is the royal cipher, here for a king

explanation.surface: A spot is pointed out on the monarch's sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A doter is someone who dotes, showing excessive fondness.

clue.text: Conference may provide growing business here

definitions.text: Conference may provide growing business here

parts.words: Conference may provide growing business here
parts.note: Conference is a variety of pear, grown on fruit trees

explanation.walkthrough: Conference looks like a business meeting but it is a well-known British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees such as pears.

clue.text: Mixture covered in caramel-angelic!

indicators.note: covered in signals the letters sit concealed within the joined words

explanation.surface: A sweet mix coated in angelic caramel.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or medley, from French.

clue.text: Held up? Put down, in fact

explanation.surface: A question and answer about something being set down.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'de-layed' as if undoing a laying down; put down in fact means the act was postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Held up means late or detained; a matter put down (postponed) has likewise been deferred.

clue.text: Choose one small part of US for seeing

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cal is the short form of California, a part of the US

explanation.surface: Picking a single little region of America for a sightseeing trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical describes things relating to vision or the eye.

clue.text: Academic honour for one of the Windsors

explanation.surface: A university title for a member of the British royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: A Windsor chair is a classic wooden chair style; Windsor is also the royal family's name, the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called a chair, and a Windsor is a type of wooden seat.

clue.text: Show hospitality to nine treat specially

indicators.note: done specially, the letters of these two words are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: Nine guests are given a special treat by their host.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain guests is to host them with food and drink.

clue.text: Opposes sister's transfer

indicators.note: a transfer moves things about, so the letters of the word sisters are reordered

parts.note: the word sister's is taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone objects to their sister being moved to another post.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to fight against or oppose it.

clue.text: Remainder live about university

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for live is placed around the letter for university

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: The rest of one's time is spent living near a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Roman's in a peculiar state in Italy

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: the words taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A Roman finds himself in a strange part of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Help to drink wine

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone is helped to a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Support is assistance or backing given to someone.

clue.text: Dismiss objection from old music-maker

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: An old musician is fired over a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is an early trombone.

clue.text: Grab below-average share

indicators.note: below means the grabbing word comes under the word for average in this down answer

parts.note: par is an average or norm
to take is to grab

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a smaller-than-usual portion.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake is to have a part in something.

clue.text: Prickly plant may appear in the list

indicators.note: may appear suggests the same letters can turn up in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A spiny plant turns up on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A thistle is a spiny-leaved plant, Scotland's emblem.

clue.text: Excellent wine given out-receiving thanks

indicators.note: receiving means the jumbled word takes the thanks inside it
out signals that the letters of the word given are put into disorder

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A fine bottle is handed over in return for gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns GIVEN into VINGE, and 'receiving' places TA (British for thanks) inside it after VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage wine is one from a single notable year, usually of high quality.

clue.text: This meat sounds dear

parts.note: dear said aloud matches the animal whose flesh this meat is

explanation.walkthrough: Dear sounds like deer, and this meat comes from deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer flesh eaten as food.

clue.text: Embarrassed not to be a real newspaperman?

parts.note: something not to be taken as real is a sham
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone is ashamed to be a fake journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A SHAM ED: a fake editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling guilt or embarrassment.

clue.text: Old tree, extremely leafy

parts.note: an elder is a small tree

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of leafy are taken

explanation.surface: An ancient tree remains extremely leafy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly means aged, past middle age.

clue.text: People are following vehicle that's pink

indicators.note: following means the word for people comes after the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Citizens trail behind a vehicle painted pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' is the noun for a flower here, as is the answer, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink is a garden flower of the dianthus family, the group that includes the carnation.

clue.text: Expect a delay

parts.note: a wait is a delay

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for or anticipate it.

clue.text: A plant initially concealed greenfly

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word plant is used

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A plant pest lurks out of sight among the leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly is the common name for a sap-sucking garden insect of this type.

clue.text: It's obvious baronet is holding back about his birth

indicators.note: is holding means the baronet's abbreviation contains the other piece
back means the word for about birth is read in reverse

parts.note: natal means relating to birth

explanation.surface: A titled man is plainly keeping quiet about his origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NATAL into LATAN, which sits between B and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Blatant means glaringly evident and unconcealed.

clue.text: Cook, hot inside, seen to glisten

indicators.note: inside means the letter for hot goes within the cooking word

parts.note: to simmer is to cook gently
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A pan heating on the stove is seen to sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmer is to gleam with a soft, wavering light.

clue.text: Scene of tragedy, perhaps, where doctors work

explanation.surface: A place of tragedy where medical staff operate.
explanation.walkthrough: A tragedy is staged in a playhouse; surgeons work in an operating room, called by the same British word.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse stages dramas such as tragedies, and a hospital's operating room has the same name in Britain.

clue.text: Twelve mad dogs out in this sun?

definitions.text: mad dogs out in this sun?

explanation.surface: A nod to the old song about who goes out in the midday heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward's song says only mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun; twelve gives the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Noonday means midday, twelve o'clock, the hour of the song's fierce sun.
